title: Topic Modeling in the Voynich Manuscript
authors: Rachel Sterneck, Annie Polish and Claire Bowern
summary: The authors fit LDA, LSA and nonnegative matrix factorization to the Takahashi transcription and compare the inferred token clusters with illustrated sections, Currier language and scribal hands. Their strongest associations were qualitative comparisons from the NMF and multiple correspondence analyses.
established: In the full-page analyses, the NMF topics align more closely with hand and illustration groupings than the LDA or LSA topics. The authors report a close association between the astrology grouping, hand 4 and one NMF topic.

The 20- and 40-word experiments sample words within pages at fixed document lengths. They exclude the predominantly label-based astrological pages and other pages below the stated length cutoff. Some associations persist, and certain links change with the sampling choice.

The five-topic and two-topic analyses do not produce complete one-to-one correspondences with the five hands or two Currier categories. The authors discuss spelling, encipherment and word choice as possible contributors to what NMF captures.

open.question: How much of the NMF association with scribal hand survives comparison within illustrated sections and at matched lengths and folio distances?
open.check: Fit an NMF topic space and any topic-to-hand mapping on contiguous public training blocks. Evaluate on separate public blocks using both ZL and Takahashi and compare prediction within shared-section, length- and distance-matched sets. Include a fixed copying-generator comparison on the same layout.
